info.title: playmatch
info.description: A blazingly fast microservice for matching ROM file hashes and caching game metadata. Originally designed for RetroRealm.

get.summary: Lists companies ordered by name.
get.description: Each entry carries the company and its external metadata mappings.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Ranges from 1 to 50. Defaults to 25 when omitted or `0`. Values above 50 are clamped, never rejected.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor copied from the previous page's `nextCursor`. Omit it to fetch the first page. Keep the filters identical across pages.

parameters.name: withTotal
parameters.description: Whether to include an exact `totalItems` count in the page metadata. Honored only on small bounded reference tables. Defaults to `false`.

200.description: One page of companies ordered by name

400.description: Malformed pagination cursor or filter-set mismatch

Up to 100 ids per request; duplicate ids are resolved once. A missing id is a

request against the rate limiter.

400.description: Empty batch, or batch over the 100-item cap

get.summary: Lists the dat files or signature groups that contain a file by its hashes.
get.description: Returns one entry per dat file, or one entry per signature group when `level=group`. The strongest supplied hash resolves the file: sha256, then sha1, then md5, then crc. Each entry shows the first and last import the file appeared in and whether it is in the dat file's current release.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description: SHA256 hash of the file, 64 hex characters.

parameters.name: sha1
parameters.description: SHA1 hash of the file, 40 hex characters.

parameters.name: md5
parameters.description: MD5 hash of the file, 32 hex characters.

parameters.name: crc
parameters.description: CRC32 checksum of the file, 8 hex characters.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Granularity of the reverse lookup. `dat` returns one entry per dat file; `group` collapses the result to the publishing signature groups. Defaults to `dat`.

200.description: The dat files or signature groups that contain the matched file

400.description: No hash supplied, or a supplied hash is malformed

404.description: No file matches any supplied hash

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor copied from the previous page's `nextCursor`. Omit it to fetch the first page. Keep the filters identical across pages.

parameters.name: withTotal
parameters.description: Whether to include an exact `totalItems` count in the page metadata. Honored only on small bounded reference tables. Defaults to `false`.

200.description: One page of games in the dat file ordered by name

400.description: Malformed pagination cursor or filter-set mismatch

parameters.name: platformId
parameters.description: Restrict to games on this platform. If omitted, all platforms are included.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Ranges from 1 to 50. Defaults to 25 when omitted or `0`. Values above 50 are clamped, never rejected.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor copied from the previous page's `nextCursor`. Omit it to fetch the first page. Keep the filters identical across pages.

get.summary: Returns a game by id.

200.description: The matched game and its metadata

get.summary: Returns the parent and clone graph around a game.
get.description: `direction` selects which slice to return: `children`, `parent`, `siblings`, or `tree` for the full graph. Defaults to `tree`. The response carries `cloneGraphComplete`: it is `false` when this game's dat file still has clone rows not linked to a resolved parent, either transiently while the background resolution pass catches up after an import or permanently when a declared parent is absent from the dat file. A client that needs a complete graph (for example 1G1R) should treat an absent parent conservatively.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Which slice of the parent and clone graph to return. `children` returns the game's clones; `parent` returns its parent; `siblings` returns the other clones of the same parent; `tree` returns the parent together with all of its clones. Defaults to `tree`.

200.description: The requested slice of the game's clone graph

get.summary: Lists the dat files or signature groups that contain a game.
get.description: Returns one entry per dat file, or one entry per signature group when `level=group`, unioned across all of the game's files. Each entry shows the first and last import the file appeared in and whether it is in the dat file's current release.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Granularity of the reverse lookup. `dat` returns one entry per dat file; `group` collapses the result to the publishing signature groups. Defaults to `dat`.

200.description: The dat files or signature groups that contain the game

parameters.description: Opaque cursor copied from the previous page's `nextCursor`. Omit it to fetch the first page. Keep the filters identical across pages.

parameters.name: withTotal
parameters.description: Whether to include an exact `totalItems` count in the page metadata. Honored only on small bounded reference tables. Defaults to `false`.

200.description: One page of the game's files ordered by file name

400.description: Malformed pagination cursor or filter-set mismatch

post.summary: Identifies many game files in one request, returning metadata mappings.
post.description:
Each item is resolved by its file hashes or by filename and size. Up to 100
items per request. A per-item failure does not fail the batch; it is reported
on that item. The whole batch counts as one request against the rate limiter.

200.description: Per-item identify results with a batch summary

400.description: Empty batch, batch over the 100-item cap, or malformed body

post.summary: Identifies many game files in one request, returning full relations.
post.description:
Each item is resolved by its file hashes or by filename and size, with the
matched game's relations on each result. Up to 100 items per request. A per-item
failure does not fail the batch; it is reported on that item. The whole batch
counts as one request against the rate limiter.

`additionalMatches` is omitted on every item here to keep the batch cheap.
Resolve the co-hashed siblings for a specific file through the single
`/identify` or `/identify/relations` endpoint.

200.description: Per-item identify results with a batch summary

400.description: Empty batch, batch over the 100-item cap, or malformed body

get.summary: Identifies a game by its file hashes or by filename and size, returning the
get.description:
matched game and its metadata provider ids.

The strongest supplied hash resolves the file: sha256, then sha1, then md5,
then crc. When no hash matches, the filename and size are tried last.

This is the v2 twin of the v1 `/identify/ids`: identical behaviour, except a
malformed query answers the v2 `{code, message}` envelope instead of v1's
plain-text body.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: The file name of the game file.

parameters.name: fileSize
parameters.description: The size of the game file in bytes.

parameters.name: md5
parameters.description: Optional MD5 hash of the game file.

parameters.name: sha1
parameters.description: Optional SHA1 hash of the game file.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description: Optional SHA256 hash of the game file.

parameters.name: crc
parameters.description: Optional CRC32 checksum of the game file.

200.description: The match result, including a no-match outcome

400.description: Invalid query parameters

get.summary: Identifies a game by its file hashes or by filename and size.
get.description:
The strongest supplied hash resolves the file: sha256, then sha1, then md5,
then crc. When no hash matches, the filename and size are tried last. The
result carries the matched game together with its game files, metadata
mappings, publisher, and company.

When the resolving hash is shared by sibling games, those co-hashed games
are returned in `additionalMatches`, ranked after the primary match. The
array is omitted for single-game results and for filename and size results.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: The file name of the game file.

parameters.name: fileSize
parameters.description: The size of the game file in bytes.

parameters.name: md5
parameters.description: Optional MD5 hash of the game file.

parameters.name: sha1
parameters.description: Optional SHA1 hash of the game file.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description: Optional SHA256 hash of the game file.

parameters.name: crc
parameters.description: Optional CRC32 checksum of the game file.

200.description: The match result and its related records, including a no-match outcome

400.description: Invalid query parameters

CloneDirectionParam.description:
Which slice of the parent and clone graph to return around a game. `children`
returns the game's clones; `parent` returns its parent; `siblings` returns the
other clones of the same parent; `tree` returns the parent together with all of
its clones. Defaults to `tree`.

cloneGraphComplete.description:
`false` when this game's dat file still has clone rows that are not linked to
a resolved parent. That happens transiently right after an import while the
deferred clone-resolution pass catches up, and permanently when a declared
parent is absent from the dat file and so can never be linked. Either way the
graph may be missing edges, so a caller relying on completeness (for example
1G1R) should treat an absent parent conservatively; retrying resolves the
transient case but not the unresolvable one.

CloneGraphNode.description: A node in a game's parent/clone graph: just enough to follow up by id.

SgdbAsset.description:
Normalised asset record used for grids, heroes, logos, and icons. The four
SGDB asset endpoints return the same shape with slightly different valid
styles/dimensions/mimes; we keep them as one struct and let the response
stream them through unchanged.

Comma-separated string fields accept whatever values SGDB accepts; the
proxy does not pre-validate the enum values, so future SGDB additions
flow through without a code change.

SgdbGame.description:

search autocomplete endpoint. Field set is small but stable.

SgdbTriState.description:

params. Encoded as `"true"`, `"false"`, or `"any"` on the wire.

SignatureGroupPresence.description:

hash or game. Collapses [`DatFilePresence`] rows for the `level=group` view.

V2ErrorBody.description:
A v2 client error. Every v2 4xx response serializes to this shape with a
stable `code` the client can branch on and a human-readable `message`. The
optional fields are populated only by the error variants that carry them, so
the common body stays `{ "code": ..., "message": ... }`.

limit.description:
The maximum number of items a bulk request may carry. Present on a
batch-too-large error.

received.description:
The number of items the rejected bulk request carried. Present on a
batch-too-large error.

restart.description:
Set on a cursor filter-set mismatch to tell the client to discard the
cursor and request the first page.
